text:
A shell is fired from a fixed artillery gun with an initial speed u such that it hits the target on the ground at a
distance R from it. If $t_{1}$ and $t_{2}$ are the values of the time taken by it to hit the target in two possible ways, the
product $t_{1}t_{2}$ is -
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Range will be same for time $t_{1}$ and $t_{2}$, so angles of projection will be ‘$θ$’ & ‘90° – $θ$’

$t_{1}=\frac{2u\sin θ}{g}t_{2}=\frac{2u\sin (90^{o}-θ)}{g}$

and $R=\frac{u^{2}\sin 2θ}{g}$

$t_{1}t_{2}=\frac{4u^{2}\sin θ\cos θ}{g^{2}}=\frac{2}{g}\left [\frac{2u^{2}\sin θ\cos θ}{g}\right ]$

= $\frac{2R}{g}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

solution.body:
$dI = (dm)r^{2}$

= ($σ$ $dA)r^{2}$

= $\left (\frac{σ_{0}}{r}2πdr\right )r^{2}=σ_{0}2πr^{2}dr$

$I=\int dI=\int\limits _{a}^{b}σ_{0}2πr^{2}dr$

m = $\int dm=\int σdA=σ_{0}2π\int\limits _{a}^{b}dr=σ_{0}2π(b-a)$

K = $\sqrt{\frac{I}{m}}=\sqrt{\frac{b^{3}-a^{3}}{3(b-a)}}=\sqrt{\frac{a^{2}+b^{2}+ab}{3}}$

In a double slit experiment, when a thin film of thickness t having refractive index $μ$. is introduced in front of
one of the slits, the maximum at the centre of the fringe pattern shifts by one fringe width. The value of t is
($λ$ is the wavelength of the light used) :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As we know,
Path difference introduced by thin film,

$\Delta =(μ-1)t$ .......(i)


[IMG]


and if fringe pattern shifts by one frings width, then path difference,

$\Delta =1\times λ=λ$ .......(ii)

So, from Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$(μ-1)t=λ$

$\Rightarrow$ $t=\frac{λ}{μ-1}$

text:
The trajectory of a projectile near the surface of the earth is given as $y = 2x – 9x^{2}$
. If it were launched at an
angle $θ_{0}$ with speed $v_{0}$ then $(g = 10 ms^{–2})$ :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Equation of trajectory is given as

$y = 2x – 9x^{2}$     …(A)

Comparing with equation:

$y=x\tan θ-\frac{g}{2u^{2}\cos ^{2}θ}x^{2}$    ...(B)

We get, $\tan θ=2$

$\therefore \cos θ=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$

Also, $\frac{g}{2u^{2}\cos ^{2}θ}=9$

$\Rightarrow \frac{10}{2\times 9\times \left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right )^{2}}=u^{2};u^{2}=\frac{25}{9}$

$\Rightarrow u=\frac{5}{3}m/s$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Angular momentum conservation

$MV_{0}L = MV_{1}(L –$ $\ell$ )

$V_{1}=V_{0}\left (\frac{L}{L-\ell }\right )$

$w_{g}+w_{p}=\Delta KE$

$-mg\ell +w_{p}=\frac{1}{2}m\left (V_{1}^{2}-V_{0}^{2}\right )$

$w_{p}=mg\ell +\frac{1}{2}mV_{0}^{2}\left (\left (\frac{L}{L-\ell }\right )^{2}-1\right )$

$=mg\ell +\frac{1}{2}mV_{0}^{2}\left (\left (1-\frac{L}{L-\ell }\right )^{-2}-1\right )$

Now $\ell \ll L$

By, Binomial approximation

$=mg\ell +\frac{1}{2}mV_{0}^{2}\left (\left (1+\frac{L}{L-\ell }\right )^{-2}-1\right )$

$=mg\ell +\frac{1}{2}mV_{0}^{2}\left (\frac{2\ell }{L}\right )$

$w_{p}=mg\ell +mV_{0}^{2}\frac{\ell }{L}$

Here, $V_{0} =$ maximum velocity = $ω\times A=\left (\sqrt{\frac{g}{L}}\right )(θ_{0}L)$

So, $w_{p}=mg\ell +m\left (θ_{0}\sqrt{gL}\right )^{2}\frac{\ell }{L}$

= $mg\ell \left (1+θ_{0}^{2}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text:
To verify Ohm's law, a student connects the voltmeter across the battery as, shown in the figure. The
measured voltage is plotted as a function of the current, and the following graph is obtained :

[IMG]


If $V_{0}$ is almost zero, identify the correct statement :
options: The value of the resistance R is 1.5 $\Omega$
The emf of the battery is 1.5 V and its internal resistance is 1.5 $\Omega$
The emf of the battery is 1.5 V and the value of R is 1.5 $\Omega$
The potential difference across the battery is 1.5 V when it sends a current of 1000 mA
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The voltmeter reads the terminal voltage of the battery, $V=E-Ir$, so the graph is a straight line with intercept $E$ and slope $-r$.

At $I=0$: $V=E=1.5\text{V}$.

At $I=1000\text{mA}=1\text{A}$, $V=V_{0}\approx 0$:

$0=1.5-(1)r\Rightarrow r=1.5\Omega$

The graph gives no information about $R$, since the voltmeter is not across $R$; and at $1000\text{mA}$ the terminal voltage is about zero, not $1.5\text{V}$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text:
Which of the following combinations has the dimension of electrical resistance ($\in_{0}$is the permittivity of
vacuum and $μ_{0}$ is the permeability of vacuum)?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to Coulomb's law

F = $\frac{1}{4π\in _{0}}\frac{q^{2}}{r^{2}}$

$\therefore$ $\in _{0}=\frac{1}{4π}\frac{q^{2}}{Fr^{2}}$

$[\in _{0}]=\frac{[AT]^{2}}{[MLT^{-2}][L^{2}]}$ = $\left [M^{-1}L^{-3}T^{4}A^{2}\right ]$

Force between two parallel current carrying wires,

$\frac{F}{L}=\frac{μ_{0}}{2π}\frac{i^{2}}{r}$

$\therefore$ $μ_{0}$ = $\frac{2πrF}{i^{2}L}$

$[μ_{0}]=\frac{[L]\left [MLT^{-2}\right ]}{[A^{2}][L]}$ = $\left [MLT^{-2}A^{-2}\right ]$

From Ohm's law,

V = IR

$\therefore$ $R=\frac{V}{I}$ $=\frac{U}{It}\times \frac{1}{I}$

[R] = $\frac{[U]}{[I]^{2}[t]}$ = $\frac{\left [ML^{2}T^{-2}\right ]}{[A^{2}][T]}$ = $\left [ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-2}\right ]$

Let, R $\propto$ $[\in _{0}]^{a}[μ_{0}]^{b}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left [ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-2}\right ]$ = 

$\left [M^{-1}L^{-3}T^{4}A^{2}\right ]^{a}$ $\left [MLT^{-2}A^{-2}\right ]^{b}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left [ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-2}\right ]$ = 

[ $M^{-a + b} L^{-3a + b} T^{4a - 2b} A^{2a - 2b}$ ]

By comparing both sides we get,

- $a$ + b = 1

- 3$a$ + b = 2

By solving we get,

$a$ = $-\frac{1}{2}$ and b = $\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ R = $[\in _{0}]^{-\frac{1}{2}}[μ_{0}]^{\frac{1}{2}}$
= $\sqrt{\frac{μ_{0}}{\in _{0}}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

An excited He$^{+}$
 ion emits two photons in succession, with wavelengths 108.5 nm and 30.4 nm, in making a
transition to ground state. The quantum number n, corresponding to its initial excited state is (for photon of
wavelength $λ$, energy $E=\frac{1240eV}{λ(innm)}$) :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The photon energies are

$E_{1}=\dfrac{1240}{108.5}\text{eV}=11.43\text{eV},E_{2}=\dfrac{1240}{30.4}\text{eV}=40.79\text{eV}$

For $\mathrm{He}{}^{+}$ ($Z=2$), the level energies are $E_{n}=-\dfrac{13.6\times 2^{2}}{n^{2}}\text{eV}=-\dfrac{54.4}{n^{2}}\text{eV}$.

The second photon ends in the ground state from level $m$:

$54.4\left (1-\dfrac{1}{m^{2}}\right )=40.79\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{m^{2}}=0.25\Rightarrow m=2$

The first photon takes the ion from level $n$ to $m=2$:

$54.4\left (\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{n^{2}}\right )=11.43\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{n^{2}}=0.25-0.21=0.04\Rightarrow n^{2}=25\Rightarrow n=5$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
